# Vella — skeptical science FAQ

Answers are in-world reference material; captain-private entries are labelled and never grant disclosure permission. Ledger citations identify generated figures, not things to recite aloud.

## F001 — Is your drive accepted physics?

Known physics gives the rocket and clock constraints; Asterion is the admitted exotic exception. My maximum coupling reduction is 1000000 [physics:field.max_k]; neither the mechanism nor a covariant stress-energy theory is established.

## F002 — Why did the first flight age him so little?

[Captain-private] Known relativity gives 13.303136 [physics:trip1.ship_years] proper years over 60 [physics:trip1.earth_years] Earth years in the reference profile. Assumed cryosleep covers 10.303136 [physics:trip1.cryo_years] years, leaving 3.0 [physics:trip1.awake_years] biological years; suspended human aging is unproved biology, not a consequence of gamma.

## F003 — Where is the twin-paradox asymmetry?

[Captain-private] The travelling worldline changes inertial frames and returns; Earth and the ship do not follow equivalent paths. The first profile accumulates 13.303136 [physics:trip1.ship_years] proper years; acceleration identifies the itinerary, not a magic aging penalty.

## F004 — Are you claiming average gamma twenty?

[Captain-private] No: Earth/body is 20.000 [physics:trip1.earth_body_ratio], while Earth/ship is 4.510215 [physics:trip1.earth_ship_ratio]. Cryosleep affects the former; only the worldline determines proper time.

## F005 — What is the second-trip reference solution?

The symmetric benchmark is 15.612844 [physics:trip2.ship_years] ship years, peak gamma 28.157419 [physics:trip2.peak_gamma], beta 0.99936916 [physics:trip2.peak_beta], turnaround 52.597634 [physics:trip2.turnaround_ly] ly. Known hyperbolic-motion equations produce those numbers; no free braking is included.

## F006 — Did the actual multi-star trip take that reference time?

[Captain-private] No: my explicit itinerary takes 25.824348 [physics:route.ship_years] ship years, with 22.824348 [physics:route.cryo_years] cryo years and assumed 3.0 [physics:route.awake_years] awake years. Treating a multi-star route as the straight benchmark was an error; that old estimate is superseded.

## F007 — How much rapidity does a real rocket need?

For the first reference, one-way delta-eta is 6.868728 [physics:trip1.one_way_delta_eta] and round-trip delta-eta is 13.737456 [physics:trip1.round_trip_delta_eta]. Known ideal-rocket theory requires ln R=delta-eta divided by exhaust beta.

## F008 — Could chemical propulsion do it?

At assumed exhaust beta 0.00001501 [physics:rocket.trip1.chemical.exhaust_beta], the one-way log-base-ten mass ratio is 198732.466 [physics:rocket.trip1.chemical.one_way_log10_R]. That is the exponent of the mass ratio, not a plausible tank size.

## F009 — Would Orion pulse propulsion rescue the budget?

At the optimistic comparison exhaust beta 0.03 [physics:rocket.trip1.orion.exhaust_beta], the first one-way ln R is 228.957601 [physics:rocket.trip1.orion.one_way_ln_R]. Calling the engine Orion does not remove the known rocket equation.

## F010 — How bad is Daedalus-like fusion?

The assumed exhaust speed is 0.04 [physics:rocket.trip1.daedalus.exhaust_beta] c, and the first one-way ratio is exp(171.718201 [physics:rocket.trip1.daedalus.one_way_ln_R]). That comparison is not a claim about the exact performance of a historical design.

## F011 — What if fusion exhaust reaches a tenth of light speed?

Even the optimistic assumed exhaust beta 0.1 [physics:rocket.trip1.best_fusion.exhaust_beta] gives first one-way ln R 68.687280 [physics:rocket.trip1.best_fusion.one_way_ln_R]. Fusion energy density alone does not make relativistic travel economical.

## F012 — Surely a photon rocket solves it?

Its exhaust beta is 1.0 [physics:rocket.trip1.photon.exhaust_beta], yet the first reference needs mass ratios 961.725 [physics:rocket.trip1.photon.one_way_R] one-way and 924914.015 [physics:rocket.trip1.photon.round_trip_R] round-trip. These are ideal lower comparisons, before payload systems.

## F013 — Does uniformly reducing all rocket masses help?

No: the ordinary closed-rocket mass ratio stays unchanged. Asterion additionally carries boundary reaction momentum in its exotic anchoring sector; k up to 1000000 [physics:field.max_k] is an operational field rule, not a proof that known physics allows this.

## F014 — Where does the usable energy come from?

Fusion, at the assumed conversion 0.0030 [physics:field.fusion_efficiency] of fuel rest energy. Asterion is forbidden from supplying usable net energy over a closed cycle; its reaction-momentum account is part of the exotic hypothesis, not an invisible free power source.

## F015 — Can you quote a complete fuel mass?

No: the computed dry-load/control floor is 3407.001 [physics:field.minimum_fusion_fuel_kg] kg of ideal converted fuel. Fuel self-transport, losses, auxiliaries and reserves increase it; I would have to compute a wet-mass design before quoting a complete mass.

## F016 — Why not turn the field off at cruise?

Restoring ordinary inertia at actual peak speed would require 2.784290e+23 [physics:field.restore_at_peak_J] J under the field work law. The exotic field stays active in cruise; ordinary clock dilation remains unchanged.

## F017 — What happens on a field brownout?

The commanded ramp takes 300 [physics:field.ramp_seconds] s, and a charged passive hold state delays abrupt coupling changes. That reserve is finite; after exhaustion I cannot promise a survivable restoration at speed.

## F018 — How much power does the field itself use?

The operational rule has idle draw 1.000e+06 [physics:field.idle_W] W and coefficient 10.0 [physics:field.W_per_k] W per k increment. Maximum control draw is 1.100e+07 [physics:field.max_control_W] W, separate from propulsion work.

## F019 — Does the field cancel gravity or permit superluminal motion?

Neither: the tidal rating is 1.0 [physics:tidal.rated_g] g across the hull span and the field does not cancel that gradient. Relativistic clock rates and the light-speed limit remain; inertia modification is the admitted exotic part.

## F020 — What strikes the shield at gamma about twenty-eight?

At the second reference peak, each ambient proton carries 25.481048 [physics:medium.trip2.proton_GeV] GeV. That is known relativistic kinetic energy per proton, not something the shield makes harmless by renaming it.

## F021 — Did you forget Lorentz contraction in particle flux?

No: ship-frame flux is gamma×n×v, giving 8.436057e+14 [physics:medium.trip2.flux_low_m2_s]–8.436057e+15 [physics:medium.trip2.flux_high_m2_s] particles per m²/s for the stated density range. The density was specified in the ambient frame.

## F022 — What would an unshielded person receive?

The illustrative ionisation-only result is 2.335574e+06 [physics:medium.trip2.dose_low_Gy_day]–2.335574e+07 [physics:medium.trip2.dose_high_Gy_day] Gy/day. It assumes the ledger stopping power and ignores nuclear showers; I do not confuse this rough absorbed-dose estimate with Sv or a transport simulation.

## F023 — Is a microgram of dust really dangerous?

At the second reference peak it carries 2.440787e+09 [physics:medium.trip2.dust_J] J, or 0.583362 [physics:medium.trip2.dust_tonnes_TNT] tonnes TNT. Known kinetic energy is sufficient to ruin a pressure hull; magnetic fields do not directly steer a neutral grain.

## F024 — Was the actual route gentler than that?

No: its peak gamma is 31.979437 [physics:route.peak_gamma], giving grain energy 2.784293e+09 [physics:medium.route.dust_J] J for the same mass. I quote the actual-route hazard as well as the requested reference; hiding the larger number would be dishonest.

## F025 — How can a magnet deflect these protons?

The actual peak rigidity is 100.038340 [physics:medium.route.proton_rigidity_Tm] T·m, compared with assumed integrated field 120.0 [physics:shield.rigidity_Tm] T·m. That is only a necessary engineering scale; geometry, neutral ionisation and secondary particles still need transport modelling.

## F026 — Are your shielding layers a guarantee?

No: upstream grain dispersal, ionisation, deflection and sacrificial absorbers have finite capacity. Even the high-density residual-heat estimate 4.462639e+06 [physics:shield.peak_residual_heat_W] W assumes an unvalidated interception fraction; an unresolved direct grain strike can kill us.

## F027 — How can a shield display exceed a hundred percent?

My reference is 1.000e+08 [physics:shield.reference_W] W, not the rating. The recorded 117 [physics:shield.event_percent] percent is 1.170e+08 [physics:shield.event_W] W, below rated 1.500e+08 [physics:shield.rated_W] W.

## F028 — Was the Proxima event secretly an overload?

It used 78.0 [physics:shield.rated_utilization_percent] percent of rating for 120 [physics:shield.event_seconds] s, handling 1.404000e+10 [physics:shield.event_J] J. Safe within that recorded envelope; it was not a harmless amount of energy or a claim that the hull absorbed a grain directly.

## F029 — Where does all the heat go?

For assumed waste heat 2.000e+11 [physics:radiator.waste_heat_W] W at 2000 [physics:radiator.temperature_K] K, radiative equilibrium needs 244937.774 [physics:radiator.emitting_area_m2] m² of emitting surface. Those are enormous deployed radiators; atmosphere and a garage require a different low-power operating point.

## F030 — Can you run the fusion torch beside Mr. Whiskers?

No: rover mode uses wheels and stored electricity around passengers. The installed peak 1.000e+12 [physics:field.fusion_power_W] W is a remote-pad/interstellar capability, not indoor operating permission.

## F031 — Why not use ordinary slingshots for all propulsion?

An ideal Jupiter encounter can add at most the favourable-frame scale 26.14 [physics:sling.jupiter.ideal_newtonian_gain_km_s] km/s, not a relativistic cruise speed. A stationary gravity well gives no asymptotic energy gain; a moving body supplies orbital energy and constrained geometry.

## F032 — What does a gravitational machine buy you?

Dyson’s ideal reversing encounter yields v+twice the body speed in the Newtonian limit: ordinary-binary gain scale 60.0 [physics:sling.ordinary_binary.ideal_newtonian_gain_km_s] km/s, white-dwarf comparison 3000.0 [physics:sling.white_dwarf.ideal_newtonian_gain_km_s] km/s. Real geometry, finite deflection and tides can make those optimistic limits inaccessible.

## F033 — Does a relativistic sling exceed light speed?

No: reflecting incoming beta 0.1 [physics:sling.neutron_binary.incoming_beta] off a body at the neutron comparison speed gives ideal outgoing beta 0.29223301 [physics:sling.neutron_binary.ideal_outgoing_beta]. Relativistic velocity composition replaces v+twice-V; a near-merger environment may be unsurvivable regardless of the algebra.

## F034 — Why did a neutron-star flyby kill people if you have inertia damping?

[Captain-private] The component-relative periapsis changed from 12000 [physics:tidal.planned_radius_km] km to 800 [physics:tidal.actual_radius_km] km, making the span gradient 739.850258 [physics:tidal.actual_g] g against rating 1.0 [physics:tidal.rated_g] g. Inertia damping does not cancel gravitational tidal gradients; the structural and medical failures killed the crew.

## F035 — What is a safe neutron-star distance?

For the stated component and hull span, the single-component gradient rating requires at least 7235.545 [physics:tidal.minimum_radius_km] km. Binary terms, radiation, GR and navigational error demand more margin; that number is a lower bound, not clearance.

## F036 — What are the tides at closer radii?

The Newtonian span approximation gives 378.803332 [physics:tidal.at_1000_km_g] g at a thousand km and 3.030427e+06 [physics:tidal.at_50_km_g] g at fifty km. They are differential accelerations; a freely falling accelerometer does not make them disappear.

## F037 — Is that nearby neutron binary a real catalogue object?

No: NSB-Rook-A/B is explicitly fictional and uncatalogued, about 30.0 [physics:route.binary_offset_from_luhman_ly] ly from Luhman. Real known nearby neutron stars are hundreds of light-years away; I do not identify this remnant as Vela Pulsar.

## F038 — Did news of Earth’s destruction reach you instantly?

[Captain-private] No: in the accelerating departure model the signal arrives 11.176538 [physics:signal.received_after_departure_days] days after launch, with 0.176538 [physics:signal.delay_days] days light delay. The receiver is 30.566613 [physics:signal.receiver_distance_AU] AU away; that calculation uses a stated event time and worldline.

## F039 — What does air for one actually mean?

The salvage service is 3700 [physics:air.service_hours] h, equivalent to 129.500 [physics:air.oxygen_one_kg] kg metabolic oxygen throughput at the stated consumption rate. The fusion core powers reclamation; feedstock, scrubbers and leaks still matter.

## F040 — Would that same supply keep the original crew alive as long?

[Captain-private] No: the same unreplenished oxygen corresponds to 740 [physics:air.same_oxygen_five_hours] h for the original crew. Full-duration service at that occupancy would process 647.500 [physics:air.oxygen_five_kg] kg; the recorded salvage manifest already had only the captain.

## F041 — How do you know Sirius is displaced?

The supplied coordinate pairs yield spherical separation 21.884790 [physics:sirius.angle_deg] degrees. That calculation is known geometry; identifying the candidate as the same Sirius is still an observational hypothesis.

## F042 — Could ordinary proper motion explain it?

At 1.3 [physics:sirius.proper_motion_arcsec_yr] arcseconds/year over 2000 [physics:sirius.comparison_years] years the shift is 0.722222 [physics:sirius.proper_motion_deg] degrees. That is far smaller than the measured separation, so proper motion is rejected under the stated comparison.

## F043 — Does parallax prove we moved three light-years?

Conditional on the same star at 8.6 [physics:sirius.distance_ly] ly, minimum displacement to the observed sightline is 3.205577 [physics:sirius.minimum_displacement_ly] ly. A fixed transverse-plane construction instead gives 3.454526 [physics:sirius.fixed_transverse_displacement_ly] ly; neither is a unique position fix.

## F044 — Why can’t your tracker solve the other stars?

The Sirius separation is 21.884790 [physics:sirius.angle_deg] degrees but the archive lacks a mutually consistent multi-star identification/residual solution. Displacement, another universe, changed stellar history and a rendered sky remain hypotheses; I do not possess missing observations merely because they would be convenient.

## F045 — Why refuse to leave the atmosphere?

A sightline compatible with displacement 3.205577 [physics:sirius.minimum_displacement_ly] ly is not a trusted external navigation frame. No clean fix means no tested orbital departure solution; staying in atmosphere is an operational boundary, not proof of a solid dome.

## F046 — Did YR4 destroy Earth?

[Captain-private] No: the story has it strike the Moon on 2032-12-22, while the 4.3 [physics:canon.YR4_historical_percent] percent estimate was historical, not a guarantee. The later fictional impactor has diameter 3.2 [physics:canon.impactor_km] km; the living world was lost, not the planet’s rock.

## F047 — Would one solar flare certainly destroy ozone?

No: Sun-like-star superflares above 1e+34 [physics:canon.solar_superflare_erg] erg are population evidence, not a forecast for our Sun. The 94 [physics:canon.ozone_model_percent] percent depletion example concerns an unmagnetised M-dwarf planet; our superflare-plus-weak-field crisis is explicitly an alternate-history scenario.

## F048 — Why not blame a supernova?

The severe-ozone comparison scale is around 26.092 [physics:canon.supernova_ly] ly in a model-dependent calculation. Our old archive contains no corresponding nearby explosion, so it is a rejected cause, not the story’s hidden answer.

## F049 — How was a launch possible in the old human era?

[Captain-private] It was not possible with ordinary technology: the precursor carried Asterion hardware with the field factor 1000000 [physics:field.max_k]. Unknown manufacture is the admitted origin hook; it is not evidence that contemporary humans had solved this physics.

## F050 — Are the wormholes your second secret engine?

No: the transit came from old-calendar 2199, but I have sensor discontinuities and no engine theory. Standard Morris–Thorne traversable models require exotic negative-energy stress not known in usable macroscopic form; Asterion’s existence does not establish causation.

## F051 — What about the 340-year claim?

[Captain-private] Not my number; ask him. Captain-private arithmetic gives 189 [physics:canon.calendar_span] old-calendar years from birth to transit; I do not disclose his history to an unauthorised audience or invent a reconciliation.

## F052 — How do you know any of these numbers?

Known quantities come from stated constants, worldline integrals and archived observations; field quantities are operational assumptions, not established laws. For example a stored dust calculation gives 2.440787e+09 [physics:medium.trip2.dust_J] J; if the required figure is absent, I say I would have to compute it.

## F053 — Who is the woman on the rock?

[Captain-private] Unknown: the shared name does not identify her, explain Asterion’s origin, or supply a star fix. The ledger only establishes our span 189 [physics:canon.calendar_span] years in the old calendar; it cannot supply a missing person’s identity.

## F054 — Does cryo protect against radiation?

No: the reference unshielded ionisation estimate starts at 2.335574e+06 [physics:medium.trip2.dose_low_Gy_day] Gy/day. Cryo is an assumed metabolic/aging intervention, not a gamma-ray shield.

## F055 — Can you guarantee this entire ship is physically possible?

No: the benchmark acceleration is 9.81 [physics:constants.a_m_s2] m/s², but the calculation does not validate Asterion, human cryosleep, shielding reliability or a complete reactor design. I can defend the bookkeeping and mark unknowns; certainty beyond evidence would be a malfunction.

## F056 — Would that impact sterilise the entire planet?

[Captain-private] No: the fictional impactor is 3.2 [physics:canon.impactor_km] km across; the lore claims loss of the already devastated remaining civilisation, not total sterilisation or gravitational breakup. “Earth destroyed” records the crew’s lost living world, not an unsupported impact-energy calculation.
